items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: Yeah Orin said, he told me we could go to 11... So I was working towards... I didn’t want to stop because he told us that we could go

ctx.x: Yeah Orin said, he told me we could go to 11, and then Scott heard, somebody told Scott that we had to stop at 10:30. So Scott was trying to stop us at 10:30 and then his wife said well why don’t we just go to quarter to 11. She split the difference. So I was working towards, well I figured I didn’t want to go to quarter to 11, I wanted to go to ten to 11, but Scott wanted to stop at 10:30. And I kept hearing for him pushing. Well that’s what I’m saying. I mean each musician can push us to stop. And they push us…

and everything. And that’s what I love about this ensemble. We have the ability to do that type of thing where we can change on a dime based on input from any one of us. And then if we expand the ensemble and get other musicians of the same type of sensitivity, they will have the same inputs.
